title: `profiler=tracy` with `profiler_track_memory=yes` allocates dozens of gigabytes during resource importing
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.6.dev [757bba192ef4c3254b44bc0d2c8cf36aa3343e30]

### System information

Godot v4.6.dev (2882965cb) - Fedora Linux 42 (Adams) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (RADV GFX1201) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 60.39 GiB memory

### Issue description

When doing the initial resource importing (e.g. after deleting the `.godot` folder) in a large-ish project that I'm working with, while having built with `target=editor profiler=tracy profiler_path=/path/to/tracy profiler_track_memory=yes`, you currently find that the editor starts allocating *a lot* more memory, with peaks of around 30 GB, causing crashes of the process or severe slowdowns of the entire system if you don't have a lot of available memory.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone wolfpld/tracy@16bac5f80790fb29ca2bd1eab903f02e8ea0732a anywhere
2. Build the editor with `profiler=tracy profiler_path=/path/to/tracy profiler_track_memory=yes`
3. Delete the `.godot` folder in a larger project (one with thousands of imported resources)
4. Open the project in the editor
5. Note how resources start to be imported
6. Note how memory usage climbs rapidly

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

None yet, unfortunately.
